name: Machine Chest Press
summary: A seated compound machine exercise that targets the pectoralis major, anterior deltoids, and triceps with guided stability.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine handles align with your mid-to-lower chest.
Sit back firmly with your head, upper back, and glutes pressed flat against the pads.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and grasp the handles with an overhand or neutral grip.
steps: Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core.
Press the handles forward smoothly by extending your elbows until your arms are outstretched without forcefully locking the joints.
Pause briefly at full extension while keeping tension on your chest.
Lower the weight under control by bending your elbows until your hands return to chest level.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you press the weight forward, and inhale as you lower it back to the start.
cues: Keep your shoulders pinned to the back pad

common_faults.fault: Seat height set too high, causing handles to press at neck or collarbone level.
common_faults.correction: Lower the seat so the handles sit across mid-chest level at the bottom of the movement.

common_faults.fault: Letting the shoulders roll forward off the pad at lockout.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades retracted and depressed against the backrest throughout the entire rep.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing the weight stack between reps.
common_faults.correction: Reverse the motion smoothly just before the plates make contact to maintain continuous tension.

precautions: Do not over-extend the range of motion behind the chest if you experience anterior shoulder discomfort.
